title: Rabbi Chiyya son of Rav Pappi
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He is mentioned at the beginning of Vayikra Rabbah, chapter 18: he and Rabbi Yehoshua of Sikhnin said in Rabbi Levi’s name that after three days a person’s belly bursts and says to him, “Here is what you stole.” Hyman calls this a scribal error and proposes as nearby there, “Rabbi Abba son of Rav Pappi and Rabbi Yehoshua of Sikhnin,” Hyman also cites the statement in Jerusalem Talmud Moed Katan 3:4. In Jerusalem Talmud Yevamot 16:9 Hyman calls the reading erroneous: “Rabbi, his son, and Rav Pappi”; he proposes Rabbi Abba son of Rav Pappi.

notes.text: The supplied וי״ק is read as Vayikra Rabbah and גריסו as belly. The Abba-for-Chiyya correction, missing Abba reconstruction and proposed printing account remain Hyman’s, without independently proving a letter history.

The consulted Vayikra Rabbah 18:1 names Chiyya son of Rabbi Pappi for the belly saying and Abba son of Rav Pappi for the nearby soul saying. Hyman proposes the Abba reading for the former. His Jerusalem Talmud parallels and account of the textual error are preserved as his report.
